newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
CANADA, Vancouver, B.C. - Oct 7 - Prince Rupert port slowly re-opening for a limited volume of grain cargoes as the new season crop arrives at west coast for export.

HONDURAS, Oct 7 - Puerto Cortes - two vessels berthed of which 1 discharging steel products, 1 loading bananas, 1 anchored to load/discharge containers, 17 due of which 8 to discharge/load containers, 5 to load bananas, 4 to discharge (1 corn, 1 lpg, 1 liquid chemicals, 1 fuel oil) no delays expected.

MEXICO, Oct 8 - Tampico, Altamira, Veracruz And coatzacoalcos affected by bad weather, which means they will frequently be closed until December '96/January '97. However, all ports working normally at present. Tampico - 11 vessels in port of which 2 cement, 3 general cargo, 1 containers, 2 coke, 1 scrap, 2 under repairs. Altamira - five in port of which 2 containers, 1 chemicals, 2 oil tankers. Vera Cruz - 13 vessels in port of which 3 sugar, 2 steel coils, 2 rice, 1 scrap, 3 grain, 2 containers. Coatzacoalcos - 16 in port of which 7 oil tankers, 9 chemicals.

PANAMA, Oct 8 - Balboa - one car carrier. Cristobal - one ro/ro, 3 general cargo/container vessels. Panama Canal - Miraflores and Gatun locks lane outages completed 2359 6/10. Approx 36 hrs delay, expected to be back to normal at end of week 42, depending on arrivals. 28 vessels due, 58 in queue, 15 booked, 40 scheduled. Oct 7 - arrivals 3 transits 41. Average canal waiting time 64.2 hours.

UNITED STATES Oct 7- Jersey City, Cartaret - no vessels. Port Newark - two vessels in port. Port Elizabeth - two vessels in port. Perth Amboy - two in port. Bayway - one in port. All northern NJ ports normal, no congestion/delays. Baltimore, MD - port working normally. Eight bulkers, 4 containers, 2 ro/ros, 2 auto, 1 tanker, 3 general cargo. 2 cables on stand-by, 4 in repair yard, 8 bulkers awaiting berths, 2 to load coal, 3 to discharge sugar, 2 to discharge ore, 1 under arrest. Hampton Roads, Va - two general cargo/container berthed and operating 1 bulker loading coal, 1 anchored waiting to load, 1 discharging grain, 1 anchored taking bunkers, 1 tanker discharging crude, 1 anchored lightering, 1 parcel tanker anchored waiting to discharge, 4 vessels berthed under repairs and/or layberth.

Colombia River - mild congestion. Up to 2 days wait for berths. Astoria, Wa - two grain vessels anchored. Portland, Or - four grain vessels anchored, 1 loading, 5 under repair, 1 container vessel berthed, 3 discharging (cement, alumina,tanker) 1 general cargo vessel berthed, 1 soda ash loading. Vancouver, Wa - one grain vessel loading, 1 alumina discharging. Kalama - no grain vessels. Longview - two log vessels loading.

Honolulu, Hi - Honolulu harbour 2 container vessels berthed 1 cargo vessel berthed for repairs 1 sugar vessel, 1 tanker loading, 3 tugs and barges berthed offport anchorage. 1 tanker awaiting berth. Barbers Point harbour 2 tugs and barges berthed, 1 coal vessel discharging, Barbers Point offport moorings 2 tankers discharging crude.

East Coast Baltimore, MD - No congestion Dundalk terminal. No adverse conditions at C D canal Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators, coal operations working well, no delays. Average waiting time Consol coal 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities normal, no congestion. Anchorage clear at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - no vessels due at shipyard coal terminal or grain elevator over next week. No delays at tanker terminals. Three vessels due by 10/11. Columbus Street, Wando and N.Charleston terminals light. No delays Georgetown terminal. Dredging throughout week. No navigation problems in harbour.

Jacksonville, Fl - no heavy berth congestion Jacksonville and Fernandina beach. Miami - heavy rain and thunderstorms expected throughout most of week. Very favourable berth availability at Miami and Port Everglades for container, bulk and ro/ros. Passenger vessels congested Mon-Fri every week.

New York - No congestion at anchorages, container, tanker terminals. Congestion in Brooklyn and Yonkers sugar terminals. Norfolk, Va - 19 due at Norfolk Southern coal pier, 2 anchored waiting to load 13 due at Dominion terminal. 3 due at pier ix coal terminal. Norfolk Southern scheduled maintenance to be completed by 19/10, up to this date one loader in operation. One vessel due at Cargill, no delays for container and general cargo terminals, oil and bulk terminals working normally. All channels opening with prevailing depths available.
Philadelphia, Pa - no port congestion in Philadelphia, Camden and Wilmington. No navigational problems.

Savannah, Ga - heavy congestion expected at Georgia ports authorities Garden City terminals due to military loadouts in early part of week. Moderate congestion expected at Ocean terminal. All liquid bulk facilities operating normally, no berth congestion expected. One to 2 days delay for bulk clay at Colonial Marine terminal due to berth congestion. Thunderstorms, vessels with weather sensitive cargo may expect some downtime. Fog may cause delays. All navigational conditions remain normal.

Gulf Coast, Houston, tx - No congestion city docks, Cargill grain elevator, public grain and Farmland grain elevator in Galveston. Mobile working normally. New Orleans, rain delays cargo operations, especially grain loading. River stage at 5 feet, normal transit times. Max permissible draft at SW pass 47 ft fw for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 46 ft fw over 100,000 dwt.

West Coast, Columbia River 14 grain vessels in river district of which 5 loading, 8 waiting. Average waiting time 3-4 days. Coos bay, Or - vessels in port 2 woodchip, 2 log, 2 linerboard, 1 nickel ore, 1 lumber discharging and loading. Some delays due to very heavy channel fog.

Long Beach, Ca - Metropolitan moderately busy for october, 2-3 days delay. Koch Carbon 3 due this month. Kaiser moderately light for month, up to 2-3 days delay for coal/petcoke. Moderately busy in Los Angeles/Long Beach for bulk cargoes.
